lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p32 - Talk about healthy and unhealthy food.

details: Talk about healthy and unhealthy food activates prior knowledge and critical thinking. Students categorize known food items into "good for you" (healthy) and "treats" (unhealthy) categories.
Look for students correctly identifying items like fruit/veg as healthy and cake/ice cream as unhealthy during the discussion.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p32 - Listen, point and say.

details: Listen, point and say reinforces the classification vocabulary. Students listen to the audio statements and point to the correct side of the poster/correct food item on the poster.
Look for accurate pointing to the 'Healthy' side for everyday foods and the 'Unhealthy' side for treat foods.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p68 - Create a healthy plate of food.

details: Create a healthy plate applies the science concept to a meal setting. Students stick pictures of food from a balanced meal onto the plate.
Look for a selection of nutritious foods (vegetables, protein, carbohydrates) placed on the main plate.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p68 - Choose one treat.

details: Choose one treat reinforces the concept of moderation. Students select only one unhealthy item to stick next to the plate, understanding it is a small part of the diet.
Look for the selection of a single sweet item (e.g., cake or biscuit) placed outside the main meal area.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p32 - 4. Show and tell with your posters.

details: Show and tell builds presentation confidence. Students present their finished posters to the class, using simple sentences like "[Apple] is healthy."
Look for clear pronunciation of the food words and correct use of the target adjectives "healthy" and "unhealthy."
